articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of Chaos-Based Image Encryption System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Researchers have created a chaotic cryptosystem based on picture encryption because of its intriguing characteristics, including pseudo-randomness, sensitivity to the initial state, ergodicity, mixing, confusion, and diffusion. In this study, we substituted modified algebraic operations between the key and the plain image for the XOR operation, which is typically used in traditional stream encryption algorithms and most prior studies, to retrieve the cipher image with evidence of the opposite action and to decrypt the encrypted image to obtain the original image, with two layers of encryption. The Rossler chaotic system and modulo addition form the foundation of the first layer, while the Tinkerbell chaotic system and modulo multiplication form the foundation of the second. The simulation results of “Pack-Signal-to-Noise-Ratio” PSNR=7.64 dB for the encrypted pepper image based on the first layer, PSNR=7.63 dB using the second layer, and PSNR=7.617 dB for the overall system. And the key space approach is 2624 for the two encryption layers.

articleTitle: Developing a Network-Based Android Messaging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Chat applications have become one of the most important and popular applications on smartphones. It has the capability of exchanging text messages, images, and files, which is cost-free for the users to communicate with each other. This work presents a chat application that enables people to communicate with each other. The application is composed of an Android front-end and back-end. The backend (chat server) and the frontend (chat client) were written using a flutter development environment, and the firebase was the DBMS used. The proposed application has a user-friendly design that allows the user to send messages, read messages, and have some additional features. The back end is based on the Firebase database and services. Firebase is a commercial cloud service deployed by Google as a platform that enables the user to develop web, Android, and its applications. The database used in this application is the real-time Firebase database, which is responsible for synchronizing all connected users and informing them of any new updates. User information and messages are stored in the cloud.

articleTitle: Improvement of Face Recognition Rate under Different Illumination by Using Exposure Fusion for Greyscale Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: In spite of the continuous work by researchers and companies to develop face recognition systems, they are still affected by various factors, most notably the environmental conditions of the images, especially the lighting conditions, whether bright, bad, or poor contrast. Therefore, Authors proposed a system that works to eliminate the effect of the lighting effect on the recognition rate, proposed image reprocessing the images based on Exposure Fusion technology to merge a set of images with different lighting, Gamma Correction and Histogram Equalization are relied upon to produce more than one image with different lighting, as changing gamma values in gamma correction can produce more than one image. These images with different lighting are merged based on Exposure Fusion technology, which is developed to deal with grayscale images to give final images with good lighting. These enhanced images are used for both test and training images in the normalized Eigenface algorithm. The performance of the proposed method was tested under different lighting conditions (good, bright, contrasting, dark, and changes in the background lighting of images) using different databases (Olivetti, AR, Extend Yale B, and Yale B databases). The proposed method improves the effectiveness of the Face Recognition system, as it achieved the best recognition rates in all lighting cases when compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Lip Segmentation for Visual Speech Recognition Based on the Convolution Process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Lip segmentation is an important process in visual speech recognition. Nevertheless, in many cases, the poor isolation limited the recognition rate. Therefore, this paper proposes a new isolation method based on the mean and the convolution technique with a special kernel to enhance the isolation process. The database that is used in this paper is the UOTletters, which consists of 30 speakers, 26 English letters (repeated twice for each speaker), and the overall utterances are 1560. The experiment results have shown that the proposed algorithm has higher accuracy (100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) with respect to the related works. Consequently, this algorithm is recommended for geometric feature extraction in visual speech recognition due to its higher accuracy.

articleTitle: 5G Dual-Band BPF Bassed on Loaded SIW Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: This research paper presents a systematic method for designing a dual-mode rectangular substrate integrated waveguide (RSIW) loaded with two squared-shaped mushroom resonators (SMR's) to generate dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) operation. The proposed filter is suitable for 5G (mm wave) mobile communication systems. These mushroom resonators serve as shunt resonators, effectively loading the SIW. The fundamental mode, TE-l0l. and the first higher order mode, TE-l02. were used for generating the first and second passbands, respectively. The proposed filter with three orders was synthesized and simulated using a full-wave simulator, namely ANSYSEDT 2022 R1 from ANSYS. The theoretical performance showed good conformity with the full-wave simulation results. Simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed filter, with center frequencies of 28.27 GHz and 38 GHz with insertion losses (IL) of 0.81 dB and 1.01 dB and return losses (RL) of 19.1 dB and 17.6 dB and 1-dB FBW of 3.53% and 2.89% for the first and second passbands, respectively. Good isolation between the two bands and out-of-band rejection suppression better than 30 dB over a wide frequency band of 30.25 GHz, excellent harmonic cancellation for,2f-1.

articleTitle: NFV in Cloud: Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Today, we are all well acquainted with the concept of the cloud, and in fact, the cloud has become an integral part of our lives, which has played a prominent and important role in facilitating our daily tasks. It is safe to say that with the advent of the cloud, a revolution in technology has been created. It is quite clear that its development in different sectors will lead to various challenges, such as security, power consumption, and how to integrate it with other different technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and so on. One of the technologies that can help the cloud is Network Function Virtualization (NFV), which improves its performance in some areas. In this study, an overview of NFV will be provided and, in addition, work will be done on integrating cloud technology with NFV.

articleTitle: An Automatic Illicit Drug Abuser Identification System Based on Facial Features Extracted
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Illicit drug abuse is very common among adolescents, and it is a major public health problem that may lead to severe consequences, such as abnormal aging and significant impact on facial appearance, like wrinkles, severe sores, and acne. Long-term substance uses disorder abuse such as methamphetamine, heroin, opioids, and crack can cause complete facial distortion, which makes it a challenging task for many researchers in computer vision applications such as biometrics and visual surveillance. This paper presented an automatic system that identifies illicit drug abusers using a deep convolution neural network (DCCN) to extract deep facia features and selection methods to select only discriminative features that contain rich information. We created new and powerful datasets for normal and illicit drug users from various scenarios. The proposed system outperformed previous works when tested on various experimental scenarios. The proposed system would encourage early interventions to prevent further drug abuse.

articleTitle: Application-Layer DDoS Detection via Efficient Machine Learning and Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks continue to pose a significant threat in the digital landscape, requiring innovative detection strategies to counter their evolving sophistication. In this study, the application of Random Forest, an ensemble machine learning algorithm, coupled with Recursive Feature Elimination as an efficient feature selection technique, is explored for DDoS detection. The aim is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of DDoS detection systems, incorporating a comprehensive overview of the proposed approach and emphasizing the importance of selective feature inclusion and the synergy between random forest and recursive feature elimination. The proposed approach encompasses dataset acquisition, data preparation, feature selection, classification, and model evaluation, offering a systematic methodology for bolstering DDoS detection capabilities with 99.9% accuracy, 99.9% precision, 99.9% recall, and 99.9% F1 score. The experiments demonstrate that the feature selection strategy significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high classification performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of SQLMAP Efficacy in Exploiting SQL Injection Vulnerabilities in Web Applications: A Case Study on DVWA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Nowadays, web applications are an essential part of our lives. The vulnerabilities in these applications enable hackers to gain access to confidential information. The most common attack technique is known as SQL injection. SQL injection attacks pose a serious security threat to web applications. These attacks allow attackers to exploit vulnerabilities in the application's backend, which can lead to unauthorized access to sensitive data as well as system compromise. There are various types of SQL injection attacks, which might be difficult to detect. In order to identify and mitigate SQL injection vulnerabilities, manual and automatic testing tools are used. One of the popular automatic tools is SQLMAP, which is used to scan web applications for SQL injection vulnerabilities and exploit these vulnerabilities as well. In this paper, we conducted an experiment to test the effectiveness of SQLMAP in exploiting SQL injection vulnerabilities. The results of the experiment demonstrated that SQLMAP successfully exploited the vulnerabilities in the targeted website. Hence, the experiment proved the efficiency of the SQLMAP tool. Furthermore, the paper emphasizes the importance of implementing proper security measures to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Improved Lifetime in a Network Composed of Fixed Nodes with Energy Restriction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: With the everyday development of Wireless Sensor Network, the use of wireless nodes has spread extremely widely. An important challenge involves the issue of energy consumption, which has been reduced in the literature using various methods. This study seeks to use the idea of mobile sinks for this purpose, where the sink approaches nodes with greater data transfer, which can thus be performed at a shorter distance. The proposed algorithm uses a sink location method in which the best locations and regions for sink placement or movement are selected due to the larger number of sensors in terms of energy. The best sink location is obtained by comparing it with the average node locations. Based on one of the four main directions and by performing sink calculations, it moves to the optimal location. If the sink's neighbor loses one or more energy levels (more than twenty levels, 5% of total energy), the sink decides to move to another point and does the same until the end. The results show that the proposed method makes good progress in selecting the next node and reducing energy consumption.

articleTitle: Hardware Resource Minimization of Triangular Membership Function Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) is today's common control and decision-making system. ANFIS is used in several applications related to control, intelligence fields, and biomedical systems. The ANFIS consists of five layers in which the first layer contains the membership function (MF), such as Gaussian, Trapezoidal, bell, sigmoidal, D- sigmoidal, and P-sigmoidal membership functions. The FPGA-based hardware implementations of these membership functions are quite difficult and occupy huge logic elements. This study implements the triangular membership function based on FPGA using five different techniques. Comparing the proposed approaches, the one with the symmetrical property, consuming 52 LUTs and 32 occupied slices, yielded the best results. According to the results obtained, this approach has the lowest hardware resource utilization compared to the other proposed designs and compared to the results demonstrated in the literature.

articleTitle: High-Accurate Application-Layer DDoS Attack Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks continue to escalate in frequency and severity, disrupting system access and network functionality. This paper addresses the evolving landscape of DDoS attacks, particularly the shift towards sophisticated application layer DDoS attacks, which challenge traditional detection methods. A novel machine learning approach is proposed using a combination of random forest, decision tree, and genetic algorithm, along with a multilayer perceptron classifier, to detect five distinct categories of network traffic, including four variants of DDoS attacks and benign traffic. The methodology involves meticulous data preprocessing, optimal feature selection through RF and GADT, min-max scaling, and multi-layer Perceptron classifier classification. The effectiveness of the proposed approach, which is demonstrated using the CICIDS2017 dataset, achieves exceptional results, with accuracy reaching 99.1%, precision of up to 92.2%, F1 score of up to 95%, and recall of up to 98.4%. The obtained findings highlight the potential for accurate AppDDoS attack detection using a streamlined feature subset, contributing to enhanced network security.

Index Terms: Distributed Denial Of Service Attack Detection

articleTitle: Effects of Annealing Treatment on Physical Properties of TiO2 Thin Films Prepared by Radio Frequency Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: The magnetron sputtering radio frequency technique was used to prepare thin coatings of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on glass substrates. The films were then annealed for one hour at 400, 500, and 600 °C. Field-Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) and UV-visible-NIR were used to characterize the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films. Utilizing the films' transmission spectrum acquired by a UV-visible-IR spectrophotometer, the optical constants were examined and characterized. Additionally, a cross-sectional picture using a SEM was taken in order to compute and double-check the film's optical thickness when it was deposited at room temperature. It was found that TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films made at ambient temperature had high visual transmittance and that when annealing temperatures increased, transmittance somewhat decreased. In the region of visible light, the index of refraction of the films ranged from 2.22 to 1.2. In the visible region, the extinction coefficient was almost nil, and it was discovered to rise with annealing temperature. The permitted direct band gap was seen to be decreasing.

articleTitle: Designing a Prototype Smart Hotel with High Security, Solar Tracking, and IoT Lighting Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Traditional hotels provide housing, food, and hospitality, vital to tourism. However, these technologies have drawbacks. Standardized service models may offer a different personalization than modern visitors want, and increased operating costs often mean higher prices. They are limited to eco-friendliness, flexibility, power-saving, and security. The primary objective of this study is to develop and execute a sophisticated hotel system that incorporates a wide range of advanced functionalities, aiming to improve overall visitor satisfaction and maximize energy efficiency. Nevertheless, there remains a need for more investigation into developing a prototype smart hotel that effectively incorporates advanced security measures, solar tracking systems, and IoT control. This is achieved by offering a comprehensive approach incorporating an RFID sensor-based door access system, which enhances the overall security measures in place. The intelligent lighting system possesses the capability to modify electricity consumption dynamically. The system integrates emergency power capabilities by utilizing a solar tracking system, an LCD screen for optimal display efficiency, and an Internet of Things (IoT)-driven lighting management system. The prototype design that has been proposed has undergone development and testing to assess its effectiveness in optimizing energy usage and improving the overall experience for guests. The findings of this assessment offer significant insights and recommendations for the future implementation of comparable bright hotel designs.

articleTitle: Novel Symbol over Multiplexing Technique for Transmitted Power, Bandwidth and Computational Load Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: This paper introduces a new technique that merges two binary streams into a single stream and demerges them successfully using the LSB bit index. The technique is called Symbol Over Multiplexing using Bit Index Embedding (SOMBIE). The SOMBIE offers a single solution to reduce the consumed power, required bandwidth, computational load, and storage space simultaneously. The merging process allows for halving the data computation load for digital processors and the transmitted power and bandwidth for multicarrier systems. The SOMBIE also allows more symbols to be stored without increasing the storage area. The SOMBIE provides higher data security due to the scrambling nature of its operation. The circuits used to implement the SOMBIE are simple and operate in parallel mode, providing a high processing speed with minimum delay. The circuits are simulated in Simulink to merge two streams, resulting in a storage space reduction of 3.125% with a negligible error root mean squared of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11\times 10-6$</tex>, which can be reduced further. The reduction in processing load, storage space, transmitted power, and bandwidth can be increased using multiple stages or by simple adjustments, giving the SOMBIE high flexibility to satisfy any system's specifications.

articleTitle: Revealing Modern Stream Ciphers Security: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Stream ciphers are essential cryptographic primitives widely employed in various applications for efficient data protection. This paper presents a comprehensive review of attacks on the Grain, Trivium, and SNOW stream ciphers, which are considered prominent in modern cryptography. Through an extensive analysis of existing research and publications, this work systematically categorizes and evaluates known attacks, shedding light on the vulnerabilities and weaknesses exhibited by these ciphers. By examining a diverse range of attack techniques, including algebraic, statistical, and differential attacks, this work provides insights into the security landscape of Grain, Trivium, and SNOW. Furthermore, it conducts a comparative analysis of the findings across the three ciphers, identifying common patterns and vulnerabilities. The outcomes of our study have profound implications for the practical deployment and usage of these stream ciphers, emphasizing the ongoing need for research and the development of robust countermeasures. By gaining a comprehensive understanding of the weaknesses exposed by these attacks, cryptographic practitioners can make informed decisions concerning the implementation and security of these stream ciphers.

articleTitle: The Effect of Vertical Members Arrangement on Temperature Load Analysis in Super-Long RC Frames
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Super-long structural frames are more affected by the surrounding environment due to their interaction with the daily temperature changes. The designers must consider the forces produced by the daily temperature loads in addition to live and dead loads and enhance the structure to avoid structural cracks or failure. The building frame responds to force analysis according to the arrangement of its structural elements. The aim of this study is to investigate the effect of vertical element arrangement in terms of their shape, size, orientation, and location in super-long buildings on the distribution of forces while exposed to temperature loads. To achieve this aim, five frames were proposed in the form of a 4story 16.0 m height, 98.3 m length without using expansion joints, and 14.3 m width exposed to a positive temperature of +25 °C (daily temperature change), modeled using the Etabs 2020 program. The methodology employed in this study was developed based on the insights and recommendations gleaned from a comprehensive review of prior literature. Consequently, the research incorporated five distinct assumptions regarding the arrangement of vertical elements within the structural frames. The first model was the basic model, and its results were the basis for comparison with other models. The outputs of the frames′ deflection, bending moments diagrams, and reinforcement areas of nominated elements were presented and analyzed accurately to discover the factors affecting the frame performance in the models. The analysis shows that the temperature forces concentrated on the vertical and horizontal elements of the first floor in all frames, as the columns of this floor are more rigid because of their fixity at the bottom. Furthermore, the reinforcement quantities of structural elements increased based on the orientation, size, and location of the vertical elements. When the orientation of columns is in the same direction as the long span of the building, there will be an increment in the quantities to 26.06% in slabs, 124.26% in beams, and 48.76% in columns. In the case of replacing the corner columns with shear walls in the frames, the moment values increased in this area (39) times, and in the case of replacing the middle columns, they increased (9.1) times. This study will assist the structural designer in starting preliminary coordination with the architects to select the ideal arrangement for columns and walls’ location within the building to save on project costs.

Author Keywords: Forces from temperature loads in addition to live and dead loads

articleTitle: Synthesis of Fe3O4 Nanoparticles from Pumpkin Peel Extract and Their Application in Microwave Absorption
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: The green synthesis of nanoparticles (NPs) using plant extracts is viewed as a cost-effective, eco-friendly, and reliable alternative to traditional chemical and physical methods of NPs production. The current study focuses on the green synthesis of Magnetite (Fe3O4) NPs using vegetable peel extracts of Pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata). The peel extract is a reducing, capping, and stabilizing agent. After that, these NPs individually have been utilized for thin film deposition on the glass substrate. The synthesized NPs and thin films were characterized through various characterization techniques. UV-Visible spectroscopy confirmed the formation of Fe3O4 NPs. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed the spherical shape of the NPs within average diameters. X-ray diffraction (XRD) further confirmed the purity and degree of crystallinity of the NPs, through the corresponding planes that matched the standard of Fe3O4 patterns. Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis was employed to determine the chemical composition of the NPs and the thin films correspondingly. This study highlights the potential application of Fe3O4 thin films as a promising candidate in microwave absorption applications, particularly for coating the gate of the microwave oven. This study not only shows the importance of green nanotechnology but also opens avenues for the utilization of sustainable resources in the development of materials with high-performance in absorbing undesirable waves, such as microwaves.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Approach for Image Caption Generation Using an Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: The automatic image captioning task is regarded as an active problem in computer vision research. The focal point of this task is to generate accurate descriptions of the content of an input image. Traditional automatic image captioning systems rely on deep learning methods, especially Encoder-Decoder architecture, and only a few of them exploit the specific features resulting from the object detection task in the feature extraction phase (Encoding) in order to maximize the accuracy of caption generation. This paper proposes a new attention-based approach for selecting two types of features: generic and specific, during feature extraction (encoding). We demonstrate how both feature types can be concatenated and further processed to achieve accurate captioning. During processing, we combine generic features extracted from a pre-trained CNN (EfficientNetV2) with specific features (i.e. object features) from the object detection model (YOLOv7). Unlike previous methods, the concatenation occurs before feature reduction, resulting in a raw and unprocessed feature matrix. Caption generation is achieved by employing Encoder-Decoder architecture with an LSTM language model. Our experiments are conducted on the MSCOCO dataset, and demonstrate the effectiveness of incorporating Specific Features, leading to improvements in various evaluation metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, CIDEr, and SPICE. Additionally, the proposed approach outperforms the baseline model in all evaluation metrics, and it shows competitive performance against three state of the art approaches in various evaluation metrics, such as BLEU-1, BLEU-2, BLEU-3, and SPICE.

articleTitle: Optimizing DDoS Attack Classification in SDN Networking via Combining Features
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Software Defined Networking has evolved as a transformative networking paradigm, enabling the dynamic programmability of network devices and redefining traditional network architecture. This paper addresses the imperative need for effective SDN security, particularly in countering Distributed Denial of Service attacks, which exploit the inherent flexibility of SDN to inflict widespread network disruption. The core goal of this research is to leverage machine learning classifiers - namely Decision Tree, Naive-Bayes, K Nearest Neighbors, and Random Tree - to discern and classify malicious and normal packets within an SDN dataset. To enhance the accuracy of classification, a comprehensive feature selection process is executed, encompassing four distinct techniques: Information gain, gain ratio, ReliefF, and symmetrical uncertainty. The pivotal contribution of this paper lies in the refinement of attribute selection through a combining approach, pinpointing the most salient attributes from the previously identified set. Additionally, a contemporary SDN dataset is employed, specifically tailored to identify distributed denial of service attacks within an SDN environment. The results demonstrate that the combined approach outperforms other methods with an exceptional accuracy of 99.9979% with the Decision Tree algorithm, emphasizing the practical applicability of this methodology. The study employs a diverse array of evaluation criteria, encompassing Precision, Recall, F-measure, and Accuracy, as indicators of performance, to evaluate the model's effectiveness. This research underscores the critical significance of SDN security and showcases the effectiveness of machine learning in countering DDoS threats within SDN networks. Through the innovative fusion of feature selection techniques and advanced classifiers, it delivers substantial enhancements to SDN security, promising robust protection against DDoS attacks within SDN environments.

articleTitle: A brief Review on the Removal of Ammonium Ion (NH4+) from Wastewater using Nanomaterial
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: The presence of ammonium ions (NH4+) in wastewater is a major environmental concern owing to their adverse effects on aquatic ecosystems and human health. Ammonium ion pollution refers to the excessive existence of ammonium ions (NH4+) in water, particularly in wastewater. It is primarily caused by agricultural runoff, industrial discharges, and inadequate wastewater treatment practices. Ammonium ions have detrimental effects on the environment, including aquatic ecosystems, water quality, and human health. Traditional methods for ammonium ion removal are often inefficient and costly. In recent years, nanomaterials have appeared as promising entrants for effective and sustainable wastewater treatment. This review paper aims to provide an overview of the various techniques and different nanomaterials used for the removal of ammonium ions (NH4+) from wastewater. The article discusses the sources of ammonium ions in water and various materials used for the removal of ammonium ion focusing on nanomaterials. Additionally, recent advancements and future prospects in this field are also presented.

articleTitle: High-Speed FPGA Realiztion of Infinite Immpulse Response Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Digital filters are crucial for navigation, communication, and modern digital signal processing systems. This paper presents a new methodology for hardware implementation of the first-order IIR filter. There are many techniques to optimize the speed of the IIR filter, but this paper uses three: look-ahead pipelining, parallel, and hybrid. The main aim of this work is to increase the operation speed with a low error percentage and minimize resource utilization with the low power consumption of the first-order IIR filter. The Spartan 3A-3N FPGA is the platform used to synthesize the proposed designs. Based on the FPGA method, the suggested system achieved the lowest speed of (16.21 nsec); it consumed a considerable amount of area, utilizing 314 LUTs, 193 occupied slices, and 64 flip-flops. In contrast, the proposed 1st order IIR filter design based on the hybrid approach achieved accurate results with small area utilization: 109 look-up tables, 73 occupied slices, and 32 flip-flops. Furthermore, the approach achieves a high speed of (9.85 nsec).

articleTitle: Natural Pollution Considerations in Designing Outdoor Composite Insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: Insulators playa vital role in the outdoor terrestrial power grid. Their performance is adversely affected by pollution. The insulator surface contamination leads to pollution flashover, causing failure of the system. Composite insulators are used in outdoor power applications due to their hydrophobic surface. Pollution types are environmental (natural), artificial (unnatural), or a combination of both. The geometrical profile design is important to lessen the pollution effect. Hence, the design must be chosen carefully, so the insulator can cope with the dominant type of pollution in their service area without flashing over. Depending on the literature, this work focuses on investigating the effect of geometric profile design on the composite insulator performance under different natural pollution conditions. Accordingly, a particular composite insulator geometric profile is recommended for each type of natural pollution. The uniform flat shed profile is recommended for composite insulators serving in areas prone to solid natural pollution while the alternating inclined shed profile is recommended for liquid naturally polluted areas. Furthermore, the end fitting sealing design is studied via electric field distribution analysis, and recommendation is also given.

articleTitle: Low-Area FPGA Implementation of Negative Exponential Function for ANFIS Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: one of the successful machine learning methods that has been used in many different applications is the adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system. The selection of membership function type is fundamental to ANFIS performance, as it has the greatest impact on the accuracy and computing complexity of the ANFIS-based model that is created. To assist researchers in selecting the appropriate membership functions for their ANFIS models, an in-depth investigation is desperately needed. One of the essential membership functions used in the ANFIS system is the exponential function. Thus, the function of the exponential membership function is investigated in this paper. Improved implementations of this function are becoming more and more needed, as the current methods have high time and space needs. Consequently, a new, more effective solution is developed in this study using a partial exponential function reduction technique. The FPGA platform Spartan-3A DSP 3400A is used to implement this method. With 28 look-up tables (LUTs) and 25 occupied slices, it is shown that this exponential function implementation provides precise performance with little space use. In addition, the method uses just one clock cycle while achieving a high throughput. The results show that the suggested approach performs better than earlier techniques.

articleTitle: Speed Maximization of First Order Infinite Impulse Response Filter Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)

articleTitle: Green Synthesis of Magnetite Nanoparticles and Their Usage for The Adsorption of Ni (II) Ions in Water
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: In recent years, the biosynthesis of nanoparticles has gained substantial attention due to its eco-friendly and sustainable nature. A cost-effective and eco-friendly technique was employed to synthesize magnetite nanoparticles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Fe}3\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> NPs) using Rhus coriaria L. seed extract as a reducing, capping and stabilizing agent. A quantity of 5 mg of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}3\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> NPs was introduced into 50 ml of the synthetically contaminated water containing 20 gm/L <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}^{+2}$</tex> ions. After the reaction, the nanoparticles were separated from the medium by a powerful magnet. FTIR, UV-vis spectroscopy, SEM-EDX, XRF and XRD were used to analyze the extract components and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}3\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> NPs purity, stability, crystalline structure, and composition. The findings revealed that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}^{+2}$</tex> ions were adsorbed on the surface of magnetite nanoparticles. According to the data obtained by UV-vis spectroscopy and XRF, the treated water sample is within the drinking water standard limits. Despite the simplicity of the application and the efficiency of magnetite nanoparticles for detoxifying water contaminated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}^{+2}$</tex> ions. The consequences of this study emphasized that magnetite NPs could be easily eliminated from the medium by an external magnet for recycling and reusing several times. Furthermore, this process could be used for the extraction of heavy metal ions on an industrial scale. Therefore, additional research is needed to evaluate and utilize magnetite nanoparticles in the field of water and wastewater treatment.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring System Based on IoT for Cardiac Care
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: The fastest-rising diseases in people today are chronic diseases, which can be brought on by various factors including dietary habits, physical activity, and unhealthy routines like drinking alcohol and smoking. In order to monitor biomedical parameters like ECG, and body temperature, and employ biomedical sensors in the patient, the design of this system integrates real-time continuous and long-term health monitoring systems. The sensors are affixed to the patient's body, and the Arduino Uno controller board processes the patient's measurements before sending them through a Wi-Fi module to a healthcare facility. A comparison is made between the obtained biological parameters and the predetermined threshold values. If the parameter is normal, it is saved in the database; otherwise, an alarm message with data is sent through a Wi-Fi module to the doctor or the patient's career, and the alarm system in the proposed system is a crucial component designed to alert healthcare providers or caregivers in case of critical events or deviations from normal health parameters. The Threshold-Based Alerts the alarm system is configured when a patient's vital signs or health data cross these thresholds (e.g., ECG too low or body temperature too high), and the system triggers an alert. The alarm system serves as a critical safety net, enabling timely intervention in case of emergencies, deteriorating health conditions, or other critical events. It is designed to facilitate rapid communication, collaboration among healthcare team members, and effective responses to ensure patient safety and well-being.

articleTitle: Optimizing Parking in Downtown Soran
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: This study examined the parking challenges in downtown Soran, a mid-sized city in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq with a population of over 350,000 and high dependence on private vehicles, due to inadequate on-street parking management in the downtown area. Soran's shortage of modern and organized off-street parking facilities causes increased costs and traffic congestion. The research aimed to identify the onstreet parking issues in Soran's downtown and propose improvement solutions. The study evaluated on-street parking conditions in the downtown area by applying engineering equations, focusing on congestion rates, the number of parked vehicles, the duration of parking, and zoning by use. Results indicated variations in parking volume and efficiency across different zones, with some zones experiencing higher demand for parking. Ten of the seventeen zones had maximum parking and maximum efficiency above 90%, indicating high demand. The study identified the challenges faced by the city in managing parking issues and recommended short-term improvements such as pavement marking, parallel parking, improving existing off-street parking, and controlling parking zones. Long-term recommendations included establishing a comprehensive public transit system and rectifying off-road parking issues. The need for a comprehensive public transportation system to reduce private vehicle usage and traffic congestion in Soran is emphasized.

articleTitle: Academic and Research DevelopmentScientific Research Center
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: This presentation examines the factors contributing to the unique success of the Scientific Research Center (SRC) at Soran University, which has combined leadership, planning, and scientific goals to create a highly specialized research center based on competitiveness and achievement. The academic and research development within the SRC is a noteworthy case of success that deserves to be studied and highlighted in Kurdistan. This experience showcases continuous and sustained progress in published works and postgraduate studies that delve into novel fields of research, including Biogeosciences, Microbe-mineral interactions, Nanotechnologies, Phytochemistry, GIS-Remote sensing, and environmental sciences. The SRC-centered research and publications were based on self-provided facilities within highly advanced specialized labs. The hundreds of publications in high-impact journals between 2014-2023 produced by the SRC and the large number of PhD and Masters graduates stand as a testament to a very successful experience in Kurdistan.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of Zinc Oxide Nanorods using Green Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: One-dimensional crystalline zinc oxide nanorods (ZnO NRs) with a preferred growth orientation along the (0001) plane have been successfully cultivated on ZnO-seeded glass substrates. This investigation primarily focuses on the bio-synthesis, specifically employing a green synthesis method, for the fabrication of ZnO NRs utilizing parsley plant extracts. The plant leaf extracts, rich in polyphenols, function as both reducing and stabilizing agents, while zinc nitrate hexahydrate (Zn(NO3)2.6H2O) serves as the precursor material. The morphology, elemental composition, and optical properties of the synthesized ZnO NRs were comprehensively analyzed employing scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and UV-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis), respectively. Additionally, the structural characteristics of the ZnO NRs were elucidated through X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. Furthermore, this study delves into the synthesized techniques and associated growth mechanisms. Notably, the primary advantages of the green synthesis approach for ZnO production lie in its rapid reaction kinetics, cost-effectiveness, environmentally benign nature, absence of hazardous materials, and reproducibility

articleTitle: Nanotecnology: The Multiwalled Carbon Nanotubes as Rheological Modifiers for the Bitumen
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering Applied and Nano Sciences (ICEANS)
abstract: The present work aims to investigate the role of multi-walled carbon nanotubes MWCNTs on the structure of bitumen and their use as modifiers for binder. The bitumen is a colloidal system where the asphaltenes (micelles) are dispersed in the maltene [1]. It is possible to improve its performances by the use of opportune additives interfering to the microstructure generally characterized by nano-meter sized aggregates of polar molecules (asphaltenes) organized in hierarchical structures, stabilized by resins and dispersed in an apolar phase of paraffins and aromatic oils (maltene) [1,2]. In order to better understand the mechanism that governs the MWCNTs action as modifiers, two different types of MWCNTs have been tested: one is a product obtained by laboratory synthesis through Catalytic Chemical Vapour Deposition (CCVD) technique and other one is a commercial one. Microstructures of multi-walled carbon nanotubes and the rheological behavior of modified and unmodified bitumen were investigated. It has been observed that the rheological properties improve with increasing MWCNTs amount. We figured out that that the defects present on multi-walled carbon nanotubes structure play a crucial role in fact it seems that these defects can anchor the asphaltenes in the bitumen creating a stable network and shifting (higher temperature) the phase transition from viscoelastic to liquid phase.
